You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

What kind of “popularity” do you want to analyze (ratings, viewers, weekly rank, share), and at what level (per episode, per channel, per series_name)?

Here are a few ready-to-run SQL options you can use now.

### 1) Most popular episodes (by viewers)
```sql
SELECT
  s.Episode,
  s.Air_Date,
  c.series_name,
  s.Viewers_m
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Viewers_m IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL) DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

### 2) Best average rating by series (via channel’s series_name)
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name,
  COUNT(*) AS episode_count,
  AVG(CAST(s.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Rating IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC;
```

### 3) Popularity trend over time (monthly viewers)
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name,
  SUBSTR(s.Air_Date, 1, 7) AS month,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Air_Date IS NOT NULL AND s.Viewers_m IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.series_name, SUBSTR(s.Air_Date, 1, 7)
ORDER BY c.series_name, month;
```

### 4) Consistency: volatility in viewers (lower = more consistent)
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name,
  COUNT(*) AS episode_count,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
  (AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL) * CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL))
   - AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) * AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL))) AS variance_proxy
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Viewers_m IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY variance_proxy ASC;
```

### 5) Best weekly rank (lower rank number is better)
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name,
  MIN(s.Weekly_Rank) AS best_weekly_rank,
  AVG(s.Weekly_Rank) AS avg_weekly_rank,
  COUNT(*) AS episode_count
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Weekly_Rank IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.series_name
ORDER BY best_weekly_rank ASC, avg_weekly_rank ASC;
```

Tell me which metric you want to prioritize (Viewers_m vs Rating vs Weekly_Rank), and whether you want results grouped by `series_name`, `Channel`, or `Country/Language`, and I’ll tailor the query.
I wanna know the min share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT MIN(Share) AS min_share
FROM TV_series
WHERE Share IS NOT NULL;
```
I also want to find the max share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT MAX(Share) AS max_share
FROM TV_series
WHERE Share IS NOT NULL;
```
